prerequisites: Basic knowledge of Chemistry, Physics, Mathematics, and Fluids.

learning_outcomes.text: Provide students with basic knowledge related to the environment, both from a general point of view and as derived from different anthropogenic activities (urban and industrial), and with sustainability.
Understand the origins and effects of pollution in different environments: atmosphere, water, soil, waste, etc.
Analyze and evaluate the impacts that these activities can produce on the environment to prevent or minimize their effects.
Study the different environmental technologies to solve the harmful effects that pollutant emissions to the environment can generate.
Ability to analyze and assess the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Possess a historical-social culture and aesthetic sensitivity.

Ability to apply knowledge about occupational health and safety, prevention of occupational risks, and machine safety, according to current regulations on passive and active fire protection, and aspects of acoustic pollution.
Basic knowledge and application of environmental technologies and sustainability.
Assess the ethical consequences of decisions to be made in a specific situation, considering the impact on society and responsibility in professional practice.
Issue informed judgments on the treatment of sustainability and climate change.
Contribute to the design, development, and execution of solutions that respond to social demands, taking the Sustainable Development Goals as a reference.

syllabus_topics: Occupational Health and Safety. Occupational Risk Prevention.
teaching_methods: Expository class (participatory master class, conferences, company visits, trade fair attendance, etc.)
Participatory class (individual or in groups. Case resolution, role-playing, technical application exercises, oral and written presentations, debates, etc.)
Laboratory activities (activities carried out in spaces with specialized equipment. Research sessions on classroom didactics.)
Integrated project (conducting a project to solve a problem or address a task through planning, design, and execution of a series of activities.)
Tutoring (personalized attention in small groups. Instruction to review/redirect class materials, learning, and work completion, etc. Specific student queries. Scheduled tutorials.)
Group work (individual and group preparation of essays, problem-solving, projects, etc., for submission and presentation in practical classes.)
Individual work (student study: preparation of readings, exam preparation, exercise elaboration, class preparation, etc.)
assessment_rules: The final course grade (NOTA_FINAL_ASIGNATURA) is calculated as: 0.5 * Written Test Grade + 0.3 * Academic Project Grade + 0.2 * Portfolio Grade. To pass the course, students must obtain a minimum final grade of 5 out of 10 points. The use of AI tools is regulated across three levels, ranging from not permitted (e.g., in exams) to permitted with full traceability (e.g., for project development), with penalties for non-compliance, including a grade of 0 or course failure for plagiarism/academic fraud.
